expected_survivors.the selection is relaxed to a subset tes: EQUIVALENT UNDER THE CHECK ABOVE IT, and I only learned that by trying to kill it. `assert_subsample` refuses first when the declared N differs from the member count, so by the time the selection is compared, |present| == n. `expected` is exactly the n smallest keys, so |present| == |expected|, and a subset of equal size IS equality -- present <= expected and present == expected cannot differ for any artifact that reaches this line. I wrote a strict-subset fixture expecting to kill it and it survived, because making the subset strict requires an inconsistent N, which the size guard rejects first. COUPLED, NOT INDEPENDENT: if the size check were ever removed or moved below this one, the equivalence dissolves and this mutant becomes killable immediately -- a subsample that drops curves would then pass a subset test. The sweep will say so, because this declaration will start failing.
